brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.requirement: Spice rack with at least three bins
requirements.evidence: Three hex-bin-full-div3 bins (bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0, bin:2,0,0), each with 3 compartments, so 9 spice spots in total.
Three hex-acc-keyhole hangers (accessory:0#0,0#1, 0#1,0#1, 0#2,0#1), one per base, all on the same back face (slot 1). The cells are bolted together and every other open face has an end cap.

requirements.requirement: Holds its load on the wall
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only. It can't tell whether printed parts, keyholes or wall screws will carry the weight of filled spice jars. That depends on the material and fixings you choose.

finish.summary: I built a wall-hung spice rack from three full hex bases in a row. Each base holds a full-depth bin with 3 compartments, which gives 9 spice spots. Each base has a keyhole hanger on the same back face, so the rack lifts onto screws already in the wall. The two shared walls are bolted together and the other open faces have solid end caps. 20 parts in all. The build check passed with no rule issues and the collision check reads clear. I didn't add props because the catalog has no spice jars.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
